reference: Niazi et al. (2017) SWMM Performance Review and Gap Analysis
evidence_accessed: Full indexed PMC author manuscript and ASCE publisher record
study_design_or_scope: Review of SWMM development application calibration validation and GI/LID quality performance; 93 publications reported formal evaluation statistics
key_findings_from_accessed_evidence: Of 93 formally evaluated publications 67 evaluated runoff and 26 evaluated water quality; 22 evaluated both. TSS and BOD were most frequently evaluated. Identifies gaps in diffuse pollutant representation fate/transport GI/LID mechanisms parameter estimation and uncertainty
limitations_or_appraisal_questions: Heterogeneous underlying studies; 2017 synthesis; detailed performance statistics of cited individual studies not yet extracted

reference: Soonthornnonda et al. (2008) A washoff model for stormwater pollutants
evidence_accessed: PubMed and ScienceDirect abstract and publisher excerpts
study_design_or_scope: Washoff equation based on linear buildup; applied to four Milwaukee-area sites and data from three rainfall events
catchment_or_region: Milwaukee area; residential/open land and mixed land use
key_findings_from_accessed_evidence: Transport coefficients reported for seven metals TSS BOD5 TP E. coli and fecal coliform; coefficients were derived using near-constant hydrograph portions around peak flow
limitations_or_appraisal_questions: Full article not independently retrieved; small number of events and peak-flow assumption require careful appraisal

reference: Gaut et al. (2019) Modelling the washoff of pollutants in various forms from an urban catchment
study_design_or_scope: Event-based calibration using six pollutants and 126 events at 12 sites
key_findings_from_accessed_evidence: Exponential washoff accuracy was strongest for TSS and weakest for dissolved PO4 NO3 and NH4; mixed TN/TP results were intermediate; parameters were best explained for small subcatchments ≤10 ha
limitations_or_appraisal_questions: Inspect full validation design exact metrics event independence and parameter uncertainty in full text

reference: Razguliaev et al. (2024) Urban stormwater quality: A review of methods for continuous field monitoring
evidence_accessed: Open-access full-text PDF from LTU DiVA and ScienceDirect publisher record
study_design_or_scope: Critical review of continuous in-situ stormwater quality monitoring; 84 articles representing 56 independent studies
catchment_or_region: 16 countries; tropical climates and low-/middle-income countries under-represented
key_findings_from_accessed_evidence: Eight parameters directly measured in-situ for extended periods; proxy relationships are site-specific; flow pairing calibration maintenance validation and uncertainty documentation are essential
limitations_or_appraisal_questions: Monitoring-focused review rather than SWMM model comparison; transfer to monsoon catchments requires caution

reference: Deletic (1998) The first flush load of urban surface runoff
study_design_or_scope: Nearly one year of continuous monitoring at single road inlets; cumulative load curves and FF20 calculated for each recorded event
catchment_or_region: Two asphalt catchments in Belgrade and Lund
key_findings_from_accessed_evidence: Measured suspended solids conductivity pH and temperature; study examines whether the first 20% of runoff carries a disproportionate pollutant load
limitations_or_appraisal_questions: Full article not independently retrieved; two similar asphalt catchments limit generalization

reference: Mishra & Botlaguduru (2025) Characterization of stormwater runoff in the Powai region of Mumbai
study_design_or_scope: Stormwater sampling over ten storm events across the 2022 and 2023 monsoons at five outfalls
key_findings_from_accessed_evidence: Reports conventional physical chemical and microbiological parameters plus emerging contaminants; institutional township outfalls had lower organic/fecal loads but elevated metals; other outfalls had high TSS BOD oil/grease and fecal contamination
limitations_or_appraisal_questions: Retrieve full text; extract event rainfall and sampling details concentration/load values and QA/QC

reference: Bhusal & Muthukumaran (2026) Event Mean Concentration-based Modelling Approach for a Large Scale Spatially Heterogenous Catchment using SWMM
study_design_or_scope: SWMM 5.2 continuous modelling with GIS and EMC nutrient wash-off; nine subcatchments and ten land-use classes
key_findings_from_accessed_evidence: Hydrology calibration R2 0.551 NSE 0.522 KGE 0.724 PBIAS 3.96%; validation R2 0.6695 NSE 0.603 KGE 0.503 PBIAS 19.03%. TN validation used 22 observations; TP not validated. Increasing EMC improved bias but not R2
limitations_or_appraisal_questions: Downstream-only calibration; limited TN observations; no TP validation; static EMCs do not reproduce event dynamics; rainfall time resolution description requires scrutiny
